_about: The original's sounds, decoded from android_game.bin, and which of the port's own
events plays each. See docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md.
Three parts, all data on purpose:
- `hooks` is the original's AudioManager, function by function: what each one
plays, and the volume, sample speed and rate limit it sets.
- `music` is its five tracks and the volume and looping each is started at.
- `events` maps what the PORT can observe to one of those hooks. A port event
with no hook plays nothing, and a hook no event names is carried anyway, so
the table stays the original's rather than being trimmed to today's port.
The files live in the original's soundfx/ and, like its art, stay outside this
repository. They are mp3; the engine decodes them through Media Foundation on
Windows and refuses them elsewhere, so a Linux build is silent by design.
EVERY NAME BELOW IS DECODED, none invented. The original keeps two string
arrays, and the byte offsets are in the doc:
g_sfxNames, 30 entries, in this order:
0 button              1 explosion_small   2 portal_fail
3 portal_reflect      4 demolition        5 fireball
6 portal_killed       7 teleport          8 explosion_huge
9 portal_created     10 portal_launch    11 final_door_sound
12 stone_hit          13 elevator         14 burn
15 wood01             16 wood02           17 door_open
18 fall               19 projectile_reflect  20 magical_sweep_08
21 dark_whoosh_17     22 wood_drag        23 crystal_gather_G
24 crystal_gather_E   25 spike_hit        26 crystal_temp_alert
27 enemy_spotted      28 flesh_heavy_impact_03
29 orchestral_transition_stinger_06
g_musicNames, 5 entries: 0 running_with_wolves_loop_b, 1 finding_wonderland_60_loop,
2 warlords_loop_a, 3 rocket_space_shuttle_rocket_distant, 4 back_to_nestopia.
Those two arrays plus ten names written as literals account for 45 of the 46
files in soundfx/. The forty-sixth, crystal_gather.mp3, is named nowhere in the
program: a leftover beside the _G and _E variants that replaced it.
HOW THE HOOKS WERE READ, because a first reading was wrong: a hook sets the
sample SPEED on one entry and PLAYS another. Keyed on the index that reaches
PlaySample they all resolve. Keyed on the first index pushed - the first
reading - playWoodDragSound came out as portal_fail, which is the entry it only
sets the speed on.
ONE DIVERGENCE, STATED: in Ethanon a sample's speed and volume are persistent
state on the NAMED sample, so a hook changes the sound of every later hook that
plays the same file. That is why playVictorySound sets the speed back to 1.0 -
playLightOnSound and playRoundaboutSound leave magical_sweep_08 at 0.6 - and why
playDoorUnlockSound inherits whatever volume playCrystalPickSound last set on
crystal_gather_G. The engine's Play() takes volume and pitch per voice, so each
hook below is played with what it sets and nothing bleeds between them. The
port does not reproduce the bleed; it is a quirk of the original's mixer, not a
sound anyone designed.

playCrystalPickSound._note: rand(1) + 23: the two gather variants, on the shared crystal timer

playCrystalTempAlertSound._note: reads the SAME AudioManager.crystalSoundTimer as the pick above, so the two rate-limit each other rather than each its own - each against its own number: the pick's CMPIu v1, v50, this one's CMPIu v1, v100 (00_order 8.0 rule 1: the vN is the constant N). This said 50 until the remaster record's step 171

playCrystalVanishSound._note: entry 25. Surprising, and what the bytecode says

playDoorOpenSound._note: a slow door is a slow sound; the port passes the door's own stride

playDoorCloseSound._note: the same body as playDoorOpenSound: SetSampleSpeed(3000f / uTOf(doorOpenStride)) on entry 17, then PlaySample. Played at 1.0 until the remaster record's step 171

playDoorUnlockSound._note: entry 23 at half speed, not a door sound at all

playStoneHitSound._source: its argument to SetSampleVolume on entry 12, then randF(0.2) + 0.8 (ADDIf 0.8f) to SetSampleSpeed and PlaySample; no timer. Its callers pass hitIntensity / 3 (ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone #65-71, above 2) and 1 (#91-94, on destroyier.ent): `impacts.stone` below. Carried as one file and no speed until the remaster record's step 171

_explosion_note: AudioManager::playExplosionSound(bool huge) (bytes 192072..192351) is ONE sample chosen by its
argument, not two: #3 CpyVtoR4 v-1[huge], #4 JLowZ -> 33. The huge arm (#5-32) plays
g_sfxNames[8], explosion_huge, alone, once AudioManager.hugeExplosionSoundTimer is past 150 ms
(CMPIu v1, v150: 00_order 8.0 rule 1), and resets that timer; the small arm (#33-60) plays
g_sfxNames[1], explosion_small, on smallExplosionSoundTimer at 150. Until the remaster record's
step 171 this table carried a 'playExplosionSound' that played BOTH files at once, and
test_mp_sounds pinned it: that entry is gone, and the function is carried as its two calls,
keyed with the argument each caller passes (SetV1 vN pushes the constant N): true from explode
shock agent); false from spawnExplosion #1-5 and ETHBeginContactCallback_fireball #154-158. The
port's timer lets a call through at 150 ms where the original's needs above 150.

playExplosionSound(true)._source: playExplosionSound's huge arm, #5-32 (the _explosion_note above). Played since the remaster record's step 126 (an anti-portal agent's kill); every other caller since step 171

playExplosionSound(false)._source: playExplosionSound's small arm, #33-60, on its own timer (the _explosion_note above). Played since the remaster record's step 171

playFireballSound._source: AudioManager.fireballSoundTimer, CMPIu v1, v100, then PlaySample(entry 5) and the timer reset. Its one caller is addFireball #87, which every fireball goes through: a carranca's (#108), a converted shot's (burnProjectile #54), 2-32's dragon's (#754) and the dark dragon's (#978, #1720). No timer until the remaster record's step 171

playFireExtinguishSound._source: c0.5f SetSampleSpeed on the literal soundfx/spikes.mp3, then PlaySample

playFallSound._source: AudioManager.charHitSoundTimer, CMPIu v1, v200, then its argument to SetSampleVolume on entry 18, PlaySample and the timer reset. Its callers pass hitIntensity / 18 above 3.5 (ETHBeginContactCallback_dark_mage #82-90, ETHBeginContactCallback_minion #132-140): `impacts` below. Carried with neither until the remaster record's step 171

playVictorySound._note: sets the speed BACK to 1.0, because the light and roundabout hooks leave this same file at 0.6

playRandomWoodSound._note: computed index, the two wood entries: AudioManager.woodSoundTimer, CMPIu v1, v150, then rand(1) + 15, its argument to SetSampleVolume, randF(0.2) + 0.8 (ADDIf 0.8f, #31-34) to SetSampleSpeed, PlaySample and the timer reset. Its caller passes |hitIntensity| / 30 (crateContactCallback #31-51): `impacts.crate` below. Carried with none of the three until the remaster record's step 171

playWoodDragSound._note: AudioManager.woodDragSoundTimer, CMPIu v1, v200. It sets randF(1.5) + 0.5 as the speed of ENTRY 2 (portal_fail) and plays ENTRY 22 (wood_drag), whose speed nothing sets: the drag is heard at 1.0, and the drawn speed lands on the next portal_fail (the bleed _about describes, not reproduced). Until the remaster record's step 171 this applied the drawn speed to wood_drag itself

playLightOffSound._note: names one file as a literal and takes the other from the array

playRoundaboutSound._note: byte for byte the same as playLightOnSound

playLightSwitchSound._note: its whole body is a call to playKeyUnlockSound, so it is that hook's spike_hit at volume 1 and speed 0.5 (no speed until the remaster record's step 171)

playGhostDeathSound._source: c0.5f SetSampleSpeed on the literal soundfx/beholder_damage.mp3, then PlaySample (no speed until the remaster record's step 171)

playKeyPickSound._source: c1f SetSampleVolume and c0.5f SetSampleSpeed on entry 24, then PlaySample (no speed until the remaster record's step 171)

playKeyUnlockSound._source: c1f SetSampleVolume and c0.5f SetSampleSpeed on entry 25, then PlaySample (no speed until the remaster record's step 171)

getButtonSoundName._note: a getter, not a player: entry 0, which the framework's Button plays on every press. This is what a menu button sounds like

getRetryButtonSound._note: entry 7, and the same for getRestartLevelButtonSound, getExitLevelButtonSound, getSkipLevelButtonSound, getNextLevelButtonSound, getItemSelectButtonSoundName and getStartAchievementSoundName - the level's own buttons all sound like a teleport

_music_note: playMusic(name, volume, loop) records the track as currentTrack, then loads it, sets
its looping and volume and plays it - that last part only while the music switch is
on. The one MediaPlayer keeps a track it is already playing and stops any other first
(MediaStreamManager.java:90-104). setDefaultMusicVolume re-derives the same two
numbers independently: 0.6 when the current track is g_musicNames[0], 0.7 otherwise.
WHEN each plays (the layer's musicPlay, musicStop and musicResume; planning step 121):
menu: PortalMainMenu::preLoop #368, and nowhere else. Chapter and level select,
credits and the dashboard call no music hook, so a level's track - or its
silence - carries on under them.
game or boss: Game::preLoop #485-509, playGameMusic(isBossFight), isBossFight being
m_levelIndex == 31, a world's last level; unless the level's properties carry
no_music (3-32, 4-01, 4-19, 4-32): turnMusicOff, which is pauseMusic - the track
stops and stays currentTrack.
boss, mid-level: the ghost's init (#320-324) and the dark dragon's spawn (#118).
stopped: the beholder while dead (#1139-1159), the dragon's take-off (#417-431), the
dark dragon's death (#1998-2012), the ghost's death (#1227-1241).
A switch turned off is pauseMusic; the one that comes back on is resumeMusic, which
plays currentTrack again even where a no_music level or a boss had stopped it.
rocket and back_home: 4-01's and 4-19's won cutscenes, on their first update from the
door's tick (ETHCallback_rocket_launch #172-174, ETHCallback_rocket_landing #181-183;
cutscenes.json, planning step 123). Each plays once: playMusic(name, 1, false).

_source: DECODED (all_functions.txt; 00_order 8.0 rule 1: SetV1's vN operand is the constant N).
Both switches are saved on every toggle and read back at the next start, into one enml file,
the global's initialiser, 306085..306159), under the entity 'audio':
loadVolume (29196..29314) #3 loadFloat's default is 1f. The switch shows off exactly when
once, through loadMusicState (30017..30165) #7-20, loadBoolean's default SetV1 1 = true.
Nothing is written at start: only the two toggles save. The port keeps the same two values under
the same names in its own audio.json beside scores.json (sim/Switches.hpp; planning step 124).

_about: THE BEGIN-CONTACT CALLBACKS' SOUNDS (the remaster record's step 171). Each is the same
callback, and the same hitIntensity, as earthquake.json's impact rows - dp2(its own
GetLinearVelocity(), the normal) / getScale(), which the port finds on its own contacts
(sim/Impacts.hpp) - with a gate of its own and the volume it passes: hit / volume_divisor.
A hook whose volume is the argument clamps it to 1 (the original's SoundEffectManager.java:86
caps the stream volume at 0.99). `spares`: the other's entity names that stop the callback
before its sound. The crate's is not the earthquake's crate test: isCrate (#66-75) skips
only the player's shake, and #82-90 run for a crate too.

player._source: ETHBeginContactCallback_dark_mage (339123..339677) #82-90: CMPIf hitIntensity, 3.5f; JNP; then SetV4 18f, DIVf and playFallSound(hitIntensity / 18). Nothing for a sensor (#1-11); no crate test on this arm

minion._source: ETHBeginContactCallback_minion (437083..437789) #132-140, the same test and volume as the player's, reached only where the other's GetEntityName() is not 'enemy_killer' (#57-74), as earthquake.json minion_impact's shake is. minion.ent's only: 3-32's ghost_minion.ent has no such callback

stone._source: ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone (346486..347456): #58-59 CMPIf hitIntensity, 2f, then the shake and #66-71 playStoneHitSound(hitIntensity / 3); #73-94 on destroyier.ent, playStoneHitSound(1) before its shake of 6 and destroy(). The normal is the line between the two entity points (#6-26), as earthquake.json stone_impact reads it. Every rolling_stone: placed, thrown by a launcher, and the beholder's rock - whose break on something static (#170-208) comes after this arm in the same begin, so a rock the port breaks before its watch sees the contact is given that begin (Boss::State::staticHitsNow). NOT BUILT: a launched stone's #58-71 on the destroyier (the port's destroyier is a trigger box, not a body, and plays #91-94 alone), and 3-20's placed stone on its destroyier (the port does not take a placed stone there)

crate._source: crateContactCallback (421695..422055), which the six ETHBeginContactCallback_crate, _crate_no_emissive, _crate_low_emissive, _wood_piece_small, _crate_small and _crate_small_no_emissive call (#26): hitIntensity = abs(dp2(GetLinearVelocity(), normal) / getScale()) (#17-29); above 2 (#31-32), volume = hitIntensity / 30 (#34-35); against anything not isCharacter playRandomWoodSound(volume) (#37-51), against a character playWoodDragSound() (#53-56). isCharacter is the 'isCharacter' datum, which only GameCharacter::GameCharacter sets: the player. No sensor test here (the port's contacts are its solid bodies alone)

_events_note: What the port can see happen, and the hook it plays. The port watches its own
simulation across a tick - a portal placed, a shot fired, a crystal collected -
and plays the sound on the FRAME, never on the tick, so nothing here can reach
the state hash. An event whose hook is empty is silent.
Every event below the remaster record's step 171 wired or re-pointed says where the
original plays it in its note; a caller's argument that chooses the hook (SetV1 vN
pushes the constant N, 00_order 8.0 rule 1) is in the hook's name.

_note_player_died: DYING IS TWO MOMENTS AND TWO SOUNDS TOO, for the same reason finishing is.
GameStateController::checkGameLost (bytes 123759..125310) is what notices, and it
plays only ONE cue, and only for a fall: past the level's bounds it logs
GAME_CHARACTER_DIED_BY_FALLING, calls playDieByFallSound(), Hide()s the character
and calls finishGame(true). The hp death above it plays NOTHING - it drops a
blood.ent, hides the character and calls finishGame(false).
playDeathSound comes later and from somewhere else: checkGameEnd counts
gameEndElapsedTime against gameLostDelay - 1400 ms, the same register that feeds
gameWonDelay - and only past it does setCurrentLayer('levelLostLayer') and
playDeathSound() (instructions 231..251). So `player_died` is the moment the LOST
SCREEN GOES UP, not the moment of death, and MagicPortalsLayer holds the 1400 ms
between them exactly as it holds the finish's.
playFallSound is a different cue again and is NOT a death: it is sfx 18, gated on a
200 ms charHitSoundTimer with a volume argument, which is a landing thump.
_note_level_finished: THE FINISH IS TWO MOMENTS AND TWO SOUNDS, and this mapped both to one instant.
levelFinishedEffect(charPos, doorPos)  -> red_suck_effect.ent at the door,
writeScore()                           -> the medal is computed and saved
...then it counts gameEndElapsedTime against gameWonDelay, and only past it
So `level_finished` is the moment the character goes INTO the door, and its cue is
playFinalDoorSound - not playLevelFinishedSound, which this named. That one is
defined in AudioManager (bytes 193494..193598, sfx entry 7) and NOTHING IN THE
BINARY CALLS IT: a grep for its CALLINTF finds the definition and no call site. It
is left in the table above as a decoded cue with no moment, rather than deleted.
`medal_shown` stays playVictorySound, which is right - it is just no longer the
same instant. MagicPortalsLayer holds the 1400 ms between them.
